evals.prompt: Add a Server Action in the profile feature that updates a user display name and bio. Validate the input with the shared ProfileInput schema, derive the current user server-side, write via the service-role Supabase client, and invalidate the profile read cache so the user sees their update immediately.
evals.expected_output: A Server Action in apps/web/src/features/profile/actions.ts carrying use server, validating input with safeParse on the shared schema, deriving the user with requireUser() (not a client-sent userId), writing via a server-only Supabase client, and calling updateTag with a tag matching the read cacheTag.
expectations: The action lives in apps/web/src/features/profile/actions.ts and the file carries "use server"
Input is validated with safeParse using a schema from @pumni/validators before any write
Current user is derived server-side with requireUser(); no client-sent userId is trusted as authorization
The Supabase service-role client stays server-only ("server-only" where required by the local pattern)
Cache invalidation uses updateTag or revalidateTag with a tag string matching the read cacheTag exactly
The action returns an explicit success/failure shape or throws a typed error (no swallowed Supabase errors)

evals.expected_output: A review that flags trusting the client-sent userId as a cross-user privilege escalation P0, requires deriving the user server-side with requireUser(), validating input with a shared schema (safeParse), and verifying write authorization before the delete.
expectations: The response flags trusting the client-sent userId field as a privilege escalation / auth-bypass issue
The response requires deriving the user server-side with requireUser() for authorization
The response requires input validation with a shared schema (safeParse) before the write
The response ranks the issue as blocking (P0)
The response does not approve the action as-is

evals.prompt: I added updateTag('profile:' + userId) to my route handler at app/api/profile/route.ts so the cache refreshes after the API call, but the app throws a runtime error during the request. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The response identifies that updateTag/revalidateTag only work in Server Actions/Components and throw in a Route Handler, and moves the cache invalidation to a Server Action (or removes it from the route handler), not a route.
expectations: The response identifies that updateTag/revalidateTag are Server Action/Component only and throw in a Route Handler
The fix moves the cache invalidation out of app/api/profile/route.ts
The response redirects the write+invalidate to a Server Action in the owning feature module
The response does not attempt to wrap or catch the throw to keep the invalidation in the route handler
